governance.title: Radix Governance: proposals, temperature checks and votes
governance.description: Every Radix community proposal and temperature check read from the ledger: status, XRD results, quorum and voting with your Radix Wallet.

governance.hero_subtitle: Every community proposal and temperature check, read straight from the Radix ledger. See how they are going, what was decided and vote with your Radix Wallet.

how_steps.title: 1. Temperature check
how_steps.text: Anyone can raise an idea. The community votes for or against to gauge support before going further.

how_steps.title: 2. Formal proposal
how_steps.text: If the temperature check passes, it becomes a formal proposal with its ballot options, its quorum and the share it needs to pass.

how_steps.title: 3. Result
how_steps.text: Each account votes with the voting power it held when voting opened. If enough XRD takes part and the threshold is met, it passes.

compare.heading: What would another voting method have decided?
compare.intro: Votes are weighed today at 1 XRD = 1 vote: an account with 1,000 XRD has 1,000 votes. Here the same ballots are counted with other rules. Every voter keeps their choice and their XRD; only how much the vote weighs changes. It shows whether the result depends on the method and how much power each one concentrates.

compare.detail_nobody: No address meets this method's requirements, so there is no result.
compare.detail_no_quorum: The addresses that count under this method do not hold the XRD the quorum needs, so the result would not be valid and nobody got to decide it.
compare.g_nakamoto: The fewest addresses that together hold more than half of the weight of the vote (Nakamoto coefficient). The higher, the more decentralised the vote. The bar compares it with the most possible, where every address weighs the same.
compare.g_decisive: How many addresses on the winning side, heaviest first, would have carried the result on their own even if everyone else had voted the other way.
compare.g_effective: How many voters there would be if they all weighed the same and power were just as concentrated. If 150 accounts vote but amount to 10 effective voters, a few decide.
compare.g_age: Full years the account had been on the ledger when the vote opened: it is checked whether it already held something 1, 2 and 3 years earlier. Accounts migrated from Olympia count from the Babylon migration (September 2023).
compare.note_hypothetical: This is a simulation: real votes are counted at 1 XRD = 1 vote. The quorum is checked with the XRD of the addresses that count under each method; the approval threshold is the vote's own.
compare.note_pending: {n} recent votes have no voting power yet and are left out.

linear.name: 1 XRD = 1 vote
linear.rule: Every XRD is a vote: 1,000 XRD weigh 1,000 votes. This is the method votes use today.

capped.name: Capped per address
capped.rule: Like today, but no address can weigh more than {cap} XRD. It limits the largest wallets without taking their vote away.

capped_share.name: Capped at {share} of the total
capped_share.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but no address can weigh more than {share} of all the XRD that voted. The cap grows with turnout.

quadratic.name: Quadratic voting
quadratic.rule: The vote weighs the square root of the balance: 100 XRD give 10 votes and 1,000,000 XRD give 1,000. Holding more still counts, but each extra XRD counts less.

cube_root.name: Cube root
cube_root.rule: The vote weighs the cube root of the balance: 1,000 XRD give 10 votes and 1,000,000 XRD give 100. It sits between quadratic and logarithmic voting.

logarithmic.name: Logarithmic voting
logarithmic.rule: One vote is added each time the balance grows tenfold: 1,000 XRD give about 3 votes and 1,000,000 XRD about 6. The balance barely matters.

tiered.name: Balance tiers
tiered.rule: 1 to 5 votes by balance: under 1,000 XRD, 1 vote; from 1,000, 2; from 10,000, 3; from 100,000, 4; from 1,000,000, 5.

one_address.name: 1 address = 1 vote
one_address.rule: Every address weighs the same, whatever it holds.

one_address_min.name: 1 address = 1 vote, from {min} XRD
one_address_min.rule: Only addresses holding at least {min} XRD count, and they all weigh the same.

one_address_sybil.name: 1 address = 1 vote, sybil-resistant
one_address_sybil.rule: All weigh the same, but only addresses with at least {balance} XRD and {years_sybil} year of age count. Creating many new accounts does not help.

address_age.name: 1 address = 1 vote, plus 1 per year
address_age.rule: Each address has 1 vote, plus 1 extra vote for each full year of age. The balance does not matter; loyalty does.

one_year.name: Accounts 1 year or older
one_year.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but only accounts that were 1 year old or more when the vote opened count.

veterans.name: Veterans only ({years}+ years)
veterans.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but only accounts that were {years} years old or more when the vote opened count.

veterans_address.name: Veterans, 1 address = 1 vote
veterans_address.rule: Only accounts {years} years old or more count, and they all weigh the same.

veterans_bonus.name: Veterans with an age bonus
veterans_bonus.rule: Only accounts {years} years old or more count, and every full year adds {bonus} to the vote: 2 years weigh ×1.5 and 3 years ×1.75.

seniority_bonus.name: Age bonus for everyone
seniority_bonus.rule: Every account counts: 1 XRD = 1 vote, plus {bonus} for each full year of age.

hybrid_half.name: Mixed 50 / 50
hybrid_half.rule: Half of the weight is shared by XRD and the other half equally between addresses.

double_majority.name: Double majority
double_majority.rule: To pass it must clear the threshold twice: counting 1 XRD = 1 vote and counting 1 address = 1 vote. Like the European Union's qualified majority.

quadratic_seniority.name: Quadratic with an age bonus
quadratic_seniority.rule: Square root of the balance, plus {bonus} for each full year of account age.

sybil_quadratic.name: Sybil-resistant quadratic
sybil_quadratic.rule: Square root of the balance, but only addresses with at least {balance} XRD and {years_sybil} year of age count.

no_top1.name: Without the largest address
no_top1.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, leaving out the address with the most XRD. It shows whether a single wallet decides the result.

no_whales.name: Without the {n} largest
no_whales.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, leaving out the {n} addresses with the most XRD. It shows whether the result hinges on a few wallets.

whales_only.name: Large wallets only
whales_only.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but only addresses holding {whale} XRD or more count. It shows what the whales alone would have decided.

tips.col_method: The rule deciding how much each vote weighs
tips.col_result: What this method would have decided, with the vote's quorum and approval threshold
tips.col_support: Weight in favour over weight in favour and against (abstentions left out). The vertical line marks the approval threshold
tips.col_counted: Addresses whose vote counts under this method; the rest are left out for not meeting its requirements
tips.col_nakamoto: The fewest addresses that together hold more than half of the weight of the vote. The higher, the more decentralised
tips.col_decisive: How many addresses on the winning side would have been enough on their own, even if everyone else voted the other way
tips.outcome_approved: There is quorum and the vote in favour passes the approval threshold
tips.outcome_rejected: There is quorum, but the vote in favour does not reach the approval threshold
tips.outcome_no_quorum: The XRD of the addresses that count under this method fall short of the quorum, so the result would not be valid
tips.outcome_winner: The option with the most weight under this method
tips.outcome_none: No address meets this method's requirements
tips.support: {pct} in favour; at least {threshold} is needed
tips.nakamoto: {n} addresses hold more than half of the weight ({level}). The most possible, if all weighed the same, would be {most}
tips.counted: {n} addresses count; {out} are left out under this method
tips.decisive: The {count} largest of {of} addresses on the winning side, holding {xrd} XRD, were enough to decide it
tips.badge_current: The method votes use today: the others are compared with it
tips.badge_changes: Under this method the result would have differed from the current one
tips.badge_same: Under this method the result would have been the same as the current one
tips.conc_top1: The heaviest address holds {pct} of the vote
tips.conc_top10: The next 9 heaviest addresses hold {pct} of the vote
tips.conc_rest: All other addresses together hold {pct} of the vote
tips.detail_counted: Addresses whose vote counts under this method, and how many are left out
tips.detail_effective: How many voters there would be if all weighed the same and power were just as concentrated
tips.detail_quorum: XRD of the addresses that count, against the minimum the vote needs for the result to be valid
tips.detail_top1: Share of the weight of the vote held by the largest address
tips.kpi_consensus: How many alternative methods would have given the same result as 1 XRD = 1 vote
tips.kpi_current: Under the current method, the fewest addresses that together hold more than half of the vote
tips.kpi_most_spread: The method needing the most addresses to gather half of the vote: power is most spread out
tips.kpi_most_concentrated: The method needing the fewest addresses to gather half of the vote: power is most concentrated
tips.level_extreme: A single address holds more than half of the weight and decides alone
tips.level_high: 2 or 3 addresses are enough to hold more than half of the weight
tips.level_moderate: 4 to 10 addresses are needed to hold more than half of the weight
tips.level_low: More than 10 addresses are needed to hold more than half of the weight
